item.title: China embraces summer inbound travel craze with niche draws, fresh moves
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-23
BEIJING, Aug. 21 -- At more than 1,500 meters above sea level, Tianmen Mountain in central China's Zhangjiajie offers summer temperatures of just 22 to 26 degrees Celsius, drawing a steady stream of visitors. Among them are growing numbers of European travelers, like Italian Giancarlo Marino. Escaping the relentless summer heat in his hometown, he traveled to China with friends in search of cooler weather. "Here you can feel the breeze, and while you're resting up on the mountain, you can even buy ice-cold drinks from the many vendors. It's thoughtful and relaxing," he said. As extremely high temperatures grip many parts of the world this summer, China is emerging as an unexpected destination to avoid the soaring temperatures. With more convenient entry policies and a host of tourism-friendly measures, the country is drawing international visitors in surprising new ways. NICHE ATTRACTIONS Jizhou District in north China's Tianjin Municipality is usually known among Beijing residents as a weekend escape. Few would expect to encounter overseas tourists there, let alone visitors from Argentina. Argentine traveler Michael visited Jizhou during his trip to China to enjoy the mountain scenery around the Huangyaguan section of the Great Wall. For him, the "coolness" of Jizhou was not just about the pleasant temperature, but also about immersing himself in nature and experiencing rural life. "The environment here is beautiful, and you can even see the Great Wall from the guesthouse," he said. Local guesthouse owner Zhang Wei has noticed a growing number of foreign visitors seeking a deeper understanding of local life instead of simply checking off famous attractions. "We've lately seen a clear increase in overseas guests. Many like to combine countryside experiences with natural scenery, allowing them to experience China in a more in-depth way," Zhang said. Dutch tourist Noa is another traveler seeking out niche experiences. On a recent independent trip to Nanjing in east China's Jiangsu Province, Noa and friends made a point of visiting local produce markets and public parks, including matchmaking corners where parents gather to find partners for their children, to observe daily life up close. "Many of the vegetables here are things I've never seen back home. It's really interesting," Noa said. China's rapid economic and social development is also reshaping inbound tourism. Slovenian tourist Rainer Grega, visiting China for the first time, said he hopes to tour major Chinese technology companies. "Many Chinese companies and brands are well-known overseas, so I'm really looking forward to visiting the headquarters of some of them. It would be fascinating to tour an electric-vehicle factory or see how those advanced robots are manufactured," he said. According to a representative of a Suzhou-based international travel agency, foreign visitors are increasingly planning multi-city itineraries, while younger independent travelers, trips to smaller cities and rural areas, and longer stays have all become notable trends. "Nowadays, many foreign visitors venture into city neighborhoods and rural villages to experience authentic Chinese life. From vibrant urban nightlife to rural revitalization, a vivid, multi-dimensional China is being increasingly shared with the world," said Wu Guoping, president of the Wuxi Tourism Association. MORE OPEN STANCE For many overseas visitors, China's increasingly convenient entry policies have provided an important guarantee for more flexible and in-depth travel. China currently offers unilateral visa-free entry to nationals of 50 countries, including Slovenia and Italy. "Thanks to the 30-day visa-free policy, you can come whenever you want -- just book a flight and go," Grega said. He added that transfers between airports and high-speed rail stations were seamless, making detailed travel planning largely unnecessary. Marino echoed the view, saying the visa-free policy was a major reason for choosing China. "It feels like the policy is becoming more and more foreigner-friendly. You can tell that China is opening its arms and genuinely welcoming more people to visit and learn about the country," he said. Data from the National Immigration Administration (NIA) showed that China recorded 22.91 million inbound foreign visits in the first half of this year, up 20.4 percent year on year. Of those, 77.7 percent were made under visa-free entry facilitation policies. China is also expanding the coverage of its 240-hour visa-free transit policy. According to an NIA announcement released on Aug. 20, citizens of Kyrgyzstan and Vietnam became eligible for the 240-hour visa-free transit policy and the 30-day visa-free entry policy for Hainan Province starting Aug. 20. The move increased the number of countries covered by the 240-hour visa-free transit policy to 57. Vietnamese student Do Thi Huyen My, now in her second year at Hainan University, happily welcomed the new policy. "I think the policy will definitely attract more Vietnamese tourists to China, especially to Hainan," she said. "For me personally, it also means my family can visit me in Hainan more conveniently while enjoying a vacation here. By the time I graduate, my parents, relatives and friends will also be able to attend my graduation ceremony without going through complicated visa procedures," My said. REFINED SERVICES MATTER As inbound visitors become increasingly diverse and venture beyond traditional destinations, new opportunities have emerged for China's tourism industry, alongside higher expectations for service quality. The city of Suzhou in Jiangsu Province, for instance, recently introduced a package of incentive measures to boost inbound tourism, offering rewards to travel agencies and online travel platforms that manage to organize overnight stays for foreign tourists and expatriates, or arrange one-day tours, with the annual reward up to 3 million yuan (about 442,000 U.S. dollars). Senior tour guides who manage to cultivate or recruit foreign-language guides are also eligible for incentives. However, experts warned that feedback from some foreign visitors suggests that information access and language services remain weak links amid the boom of inbound tourism, which underscores the need to improve tourism services for international guests. Wu Guoping suggested building a more comprehensive support system by developing multilingual digital platforms that seamlessly connect transportation, accommodation, dining, shopping and attractions, making travel planning and consumption more convenient. To that end, Shanghai has recently launched a type of integrated smart tourism service kiosk that combines abundant online and offline resources. Resembling a telephone booth, the facility provides access to 14,000 ticketing and shopping links, more than 20,000 dining venues and over 7,500 hotels and guesthouses. Powered by an AI travel assistant, it offers personalized recommendations, real-time interpretation and AI-generated travel journals. Its foreign bank card payment system supports 10 languages and more than 120 currencies. Zhangjiajie is also improving services to match its surging international guests. From January to July this year, the city received 860,700 inbound visitors from 195 countries and regions, up 19.01 percent year on year. Tourism foreign exchange revenue reached 98.52 million U.S. dollars, an increase of 40.52 percent. Despite the rapid growth, a previous survey in the Wulingyuan Scenic Area found that fewer than one-third of frontline staff could communicate proficiently in a foreign language. The scenic area has since partnered with local universities to compile English-, Korean- and other foreign-language learning handbooks, while organizing evening classes for tourism workers. Chen Heng, a 52-year-old publicity officer and one of the evening school participants, has even purchased language-learning software at his own expense and practices English pronunciation by reading aloud with a chopstick in his mouth. "Zhangjiajie boasts world-class natural scenery. Our service quality has to keep pace as well," he said.

item.title: Chinese vice premier stresses disaster control efforts to ensure bumper harvest
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-22
BEIJING, Aug. 21 -- Chinese Vice Premier Liu Guozhong has stressed the need to step up disaster prevention and mitigation in agricultural production and make every effort to secure a bumper harvest this year. Liu, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks Friday during a video conference at the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs on autumn grain production and disaster control. He called for close monitoring of potential disasters, timely forecasts and early warnings, and targeted technical guidance. All measures to stabilize and increase grain yields should be implemented, he noted. Strong efforts should be made to guard against and respond to meteorological disasters, crop diseases and pests in the latter stages of autumn grain production, and minimize disaster-related losses, Liu said. Timely assistance should be provided to households at risk of falling or relapsing into poverty due to disasters, he said, calling for continued efforts to improve farmland irrigation and drainage channels and strengthen the management of flood-prone areas on plains. Post-disaster agricultural production should be restored in light of local conditions, and the development of high-standard farmland should be advanced with high quality, according to the vice premier. Liu also visited Hebei Province on Thursday to inspect autumn grain growth, high-standard farmland development, agricultural supplies and weather services for agriculture.

item.title: China's top anti-graft body vows higher standards, more concrete measures to advance its work
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-22
BEIJING, Aug. 22 -- The sixth plenary session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (CCDI) of the Communist Party of China (CPC) was held in Beijing on Saturday. Li Xi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and secretary of the CCDI, addressed the session. The session called for steadfastly following the Chinese path to combat corruption and advance the high-quality development of discipline inspection and supervision work in the new era, with higher standards and more concrete measures. The session reviewed discipline inspection and supervision work in the first half of 2026 and made further arrangements to ensure the effective implementation of relevant tasks. It called for strengthening political oversight, deepening political inspections, strictly enforcing discipline in leadership transitions, unswervingly improving conduct, enforcing discipline and combating corruption, and continuing concentrated rectification of misconduct and corruption at the people's doorsteps, to ensure the high-quality completion of all tasks for the year. The session elected Zhao Shiyong deputy secretary of the CCDI, and Zhang Zhong deputy secretary of the CCDI and a member of its Standing Committee.

item.title: Chinese state councilor calls for faster development of youth football system
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-21
BEIJING, Aug. 21 -- Chinese State Councilor Shen Yiqin has urged greater efforts to develop youth football and train future elite athletes as part of a broader push to strengthen the foundation of Chinese football. Shen made the remarks during a visit to youth football facilities in Beijing on Thursday, where she focused on the development of the youth football system. Shen visited the Beijing Youth Football Training Center and watched the Baidui Cup, one of the capital's major youth football tournaments. She said sustained efforts to develop youth football were needed to build a stronger foundation for the revitalization of Chinese football. China should accelerate the construction of youth training centers at all levels, Shen said. She called for stronger coaching systems, expanded campus football programs and an improved competition structure, while stressing the importance of sports ethics and discipline. She also urged greater efforts to develop more elite players. China has made youth development a priority in its long-running effort to improve football standards, with grassroots training viewed as a key area for producing internationally competitive players. Shen also visited Xiannongtan Sports School, where she stressed the need to deepen the integration of sports and education. She called for better coordination between academic studies and athletic training to develop more well-rounded athletes for competitive sports.

item.title: Chinese premier chairs State Council executive meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-21
BEIJING, Aug. 21 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Friday chaired a State Council executive meeting that heard a report on the development of next-generation communication networks and made arrangements for further efforts to clear overdue payments owed to enterprises. The meeting discussed measures to further improve air quality, adopted draft revisions to regulations on emergency response and investigation of power safety accidents, and approved draft regulations on market regulation offices at township level. China will coordinate the development of terrestrial, space-based, international and integrated networks, while promoting wider use of next-generation smart devices and developing high-value applications in areas such as smart cities and intelligent manufacturing, the meeting said. It also called for stronger protection of critical network infrastructure and data security, improved emergency communications, and better support for the use of land, electricity and spectrum resources. The meeting urged stepped-up efforts to clear overdue payments to businesses and guide local authorities in making better use of policy tools such as special-purpose bonds and special relending facilities. It also emphasized stronger enforcement against unfair competition and better regulation of non-cash payment instruments. Efforts should continue to improve air quality, with stronger support from fiscal, financial and pricing policies, and promote greener production and lifestyles, the meeting said. It called for stronger maintenance and safety checks of power equipment and facilities, tighter quality control throughout the design, construction and acceptance of new projects, and improved emergency response capabilities for power safety accidents. The meeting also urged greater use of technology to improve market regulation and public services and safeguard a fair and orderly market environment.

item.title: Xi calls for stronger China-Ecuador synergy in development strategies
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-19
BEIJING, Aug. 18 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday emphasized that China and Ecuador should strengthen the synergy of their development strategies and implement the cooperation plan for jointly building the Belt and Road. The two countries should deliver on cooperation projects in energy, minerals, infrastructure, finance and other sectors, and actively explore cooperation in areas including the digital economy, green development, new energy and artificial intelligence, Xi said when holding talks with President of the Republic of Ecuador Daniel Roy-Gilchrist Noboa Azín in Beijing. Noboa is on a state visit to China from Aug. 16 to 23 at the invitation of Xi. Noting this year marks the 10th anniversary of the China-Ecuador comprehensive strategic partnership, Xi said no matter how the international landscape changes, China has always viewed China-Ecuador relations from a strategic and long-term perspective. China stands ready to work with Ecuador to continuously elevate bilateral relations to new heights and deliver greater benefits to the people of both countries, he said. Xi said China respects and supports Ecuador in exploring a development path that suits its national conditions. China is willing to intensify exchanges between the two countries across various sectors, including governments, legislatures, and political parties, and enhance experience sharing on governance, he added. The Chinese president encouraged both sides to continue unlocking the potential of the free trade agreement so that its dividends can benefit more businesses and consumers. He also expressed China's willingness to cooperate with Ecuador in areas such as healthcare, poverty alleviation, disaster prevention and mitigation, in support of Ecuador's national development. Calling China an important partner and friend of Ecuador, Noboa said bilateral relations have entered a new phase, delivering tangible benefits to the two peoples. He said Ecuador is willing to deepen political mutual trust with China, supports China in safeguarding its sovereignty and territorial integrity, and respects China's position on the Taiwan question. Noting that Ecuador attaches great importance to cooperation with China, Noboa called on the two sides to strengthen mutually beneficial cooperation in economy and trade, finance, minerals, renewable energy, science and technology, culture and other fields. Ecuador will expand its exports to China, and welcomes more Chinese enterprises to invest and operate in Ecuador, which is expected to help improve the well-being of the people and facilitate the development of the country, he added. The two heads of state exchanged views on the situation in the Latin American and Caribbean region. Xi said China supports Latin American countries in upholding independence and self-reliance, pursuing foreign cooperation based on their national interests, and safeguarding regional peace and stability. Xi stressed that China has always maintained that the status of the Latin American and Caribbean region as a zone of peace should not be undermined, the course of development and revitalization of Latin American and Caribbean countries should not be disrupted, and the right of Latin American and Caribbean countries to independently choose their cooperation partners should not be interfered with. Noting Ecuador highly values China's position and role, Noboa said Ecuador is always willing to be a good friend of China on the other side of the Pacific Ocean. After the talks, the two heads of state attended a signing ceremony for multiple cooperation agreements in areas such as green industry, economic and trade cooperation, the digital economy and people's livelihood. Prior to the talks in the Great Hall of the People, Xi held a welcome ceremony for Noboa. Xi also hosted a welcome banquet for him in the evening.

item.title: China to revise regulations on housing provident fund management
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-18
BEIJING, Aug. 18 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree publicizing a decision to revise the Regulations on Management of Housing Provident Fund, which will take effect on Sept. 20, 2026. According to the decision, the scope of the fund's withdrawal and use will be expanded. For those withdrawing from the housing provident fund to pay rent, the eligibility threshold requiring rent to exceed a prescribed proportion of a household's wage income will be removed. Housing provident fund savings can be withdrawn for new purposes under the revised regulations, including renovating the homes the contributors live in and paying property management fees for such homes. The decision also states that the channels for the investment and utilization of the housing provident fund will be appropriately broadened, specifying that housing provident fund management centers are allowed to use the funds to purchase policy-oriented financial bonds. To enhance the efficiency of management services, the decision also underscores efforts to simplify the procedures for employees to apply for housing provident fund withdrawals and to shorten the review period for housing provident fund loan applications. The decision, which strengthens risk prevention and control, stipulates that housing provident fund management centers should establish comprehensive, complete and accurate credit records and incorporate them into the national credit information sharing platform. Amid efforts to expand the coverage of the system, the decision clarifies that individual business owners, part-time employees and other people in flexible employment can pay voluntary contributions into the housing provident fund and enjoy policy support in accordance with the regulations.

item.title: China issues new five-year plan on public legal education
item.description:
Published: 2026-07-28
BEIJING, July 27 -- China has unveiled a new five-year plan to strengthen public legal education and promote the rule of law, with the aim of creating a favorable legal environment for the country's modernization drive. The 2026-2030 plan, the ninth of its kind, is formulated by the Publicity Department of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the Ministry of Justice. It calls for improving officials' ability to govern in accordance with the law and enhancing citizens' legal awareness to foster a culture that respects the law, observes rules, honors contracts and upholds fairness. By the end of the decade, public legal education is expected to become more institutionalized, standardized and technology-enabled, the plan said. The document places strong emphasis on legal awareness in areas related to business and innovation. It calls for broader public education on laws governing the business environment, the private economy, the digital economy and intellectual property protection. The plan also seeks greater awareness of financial regulations to better protect consumers and investors while helping prevent and mitigate financial risks. As China pursues higher-standard opening up, the plan highlights laws and regulations related to foreign trade, cross-border investment, international commercial dispute resolution, and cross-border travel. Beyond the economy, the plan aims to expand legal education in areas closely tied to daily life, as well as to environmental protection, personal data security, and the prevention of telecom and online fraud.
